baslik: The Reservoir That Overfilled Because Its Sensors Came Loose

sahneler.metin: Before dawn, a mountaintop reservoir in Missouri burst its wall.
Within minutes, a billion gallons of water rushed down the mountain.
Pumps had kept filling it past full.
Its water level sensors had come loose.
They reported a lower level than the real one.
A backup sensor was set too high to help.
Water spilled over the wall and eroded it.
The rebuilt reservoir has independent overfill protection.

aciklama:
Taum Sauk overflowed and breached its wall. The cause: pumping continued past full because level sensors read low, overtopping and eroding the embankment.
